items.name: Phones & Tablets
items.intro: Phones lose value fastest in their first year, then settle into a predictable slope. The two things that decide a used phone's price are whether it is locked (carrier, activation or finance lock) and battery health.
buy: Meet where you can test on Wi-Fi and a SIM — a phone shop or police-station exchange zone.
Check the IMEI/serial against carrier blacklist and finance status before paying.
Confirm it shows the setup 'Hello' screen after reset, or that the seller signs out of their account in front of you.
Read battery health in settings; below ~80% means a replacement is due soon.
Test cameras, speakers, mic, Face/Touch ID, charging port and every button.
sell: Back up, sign out of iCloud/Google, remove the SIM and eSIM, then factory reset.
Photograph the screen on, battery-health screen and IMEI screen.
Include the box and original cable: complete sets typically sell faster.
Price against recent sold listings, not asking prices.
For speed over price, compare an instant buyback quote with a P2P listing.
flags: Seller can't show the device powered on or unlocked
Price far below every comparable sold listing
Pressure to pay before inspection
Refuses an IMEI check
check: Not activation-locked / signed out of owner account
IMEI clean (not blacklisted, not under finance)
Screen: no dead pixels, burn-in or touch dead zones
Charging port charges with your cable
No swelling: phone lies flat, no screen lift
Model and storage match the listing

items.name: Laptops & Computers
items.intro: Laptops hold value when they are recent, upgraded and cleanly reset. Firmware or management locks are the single biggest risk for buyers.
buy: Ask the seller to boot to the login screen and then to setup after a reset in front of you.
Check for firmware/BIOS passwords and remote-management (MDM) enrolment.
Run a battery cycle-count and health check.
Test every port, keyboard key, trackpad, webcam and Wi-Fi.
Match the serial number to the model, CPU, RAM and storage advertised.
sell: Back up, sign out of every account, disable 'Find My', wipe and reinstall the OS.
List exact specs: CPU, RAM, storage, screen, battery cycles.
Clean the keyboard and screen — photos sell the condition.
Include the original charger; missing chargers cut offers.
flags: 'Forgot the password' or 'just needs a reset'
Firmware lock or 'managed by organization' notice
Serial number scratched off
check: Boots to setup after reset — no account lock
Battery health and cycle count acceptable
Display: no dead pixels, backlight bleed or lines

items.name: Consoles & Games
items.intro: Consoles depreciate gently, and retro hardware often appreciates. Bans, drift and overheating are the hidden costs.
buy: See it running a game, not just the menu.
Check controllers for stick drift and trigger response.
Ask whether the console is account-banned from online play.
Listen for loud fans and check for overheating smells.
sell: Deregister/deactivate as primary console and factory reset.
Bundle controllers and games — bundles sell faster locally.
Retro games: photograph labels, manuals and cartridge pins.
flags: Won't show it running
Sealed 'new' console far below retail from a new account
check: Powers on and runs a game

items.name: Cars & Vehicles
items.intro: A used car is the largest used purchase most people make. Title status, accident history and an independent mechanical inspection matter more than the price.
buy: Run the VIN through a vehicle-history service and check open recalls.
Get a pre-purchase inspection from an independent mechanic.
Make sure the name on the title matches the seller's ID and there are no liens.
Test drive cold, on the highway, and over bumps.
Pay by bank-verified method at a bank, never by gift card or wire to a stranger.
sell: Gather title, service records and spare keys.
Detail it: clean cars photograph and sell better.
Know your number: compare trade-in, private-party and instant offers.
Meet at your bank or a police-station exchange zone; verify funds before signing over.
flags: Seller 'overseas' or 'deployed' who will ship the car
Title not in seller's name
Asks for payment via gift cards or escrow site they choose
Price far below market
check: VIN matches title, dash and door jamb
No liens; seller's ID matches title
Cold start: no smoke, knocks or warning lights
Fluids: no milky oil, low or dirty coolant
Panel gaps and paint match (accident signs)

items.name: Bikes & E-bikes
items.intro: Bicycles are a stolen-goods hotspot, and e-bike batteries are the costliest hidden risk. Check both before money changes hands.
buy: Search the serial number in a stolen-bike registry.
Check frame and fork for cracks, especially carbon.
For e-bikes: check battery age, charger and recalls; avoid swollen or damaged packs.
Ride it: shifting, brakes, bearings.
sell: Record the serial number and register the sale.
Tune-up and clean drivetrain before photos.
Include battery charge cycles and charger for e-bikes.
flags: Seller can't explain where the bike came from
No battery charger or mismatched charger
Ground-off serial number
check: Serial number present and not reported stolen
E-bike battery: no swelling, damage or recall
Frame and fork: no cracks or bends

items.name: Furniture
items.intro: Mass-market furniture loses most of its value on day one; solid wood, designer and vintage pieces hold or gain. Logistics — not price — usually decide where to sell.
buy: Check for bed bugs on seams and joints of upholstered pieces.
Measure your doors, stairs and space before you go.
Sit, open, lean: test joints, drawers and mechanisms.
Plan transport before paying.
sell: Name the brand and model — brand names are search terms.
Give exact dimensions and photograph in daylight.
For heavy items, local pickup or a managed marketplace beats shipping.
flags: Upholstery with dark spotting on seams
Seller rushes you past inspecting
check: No signs of bed bugs or pests
Frame solid — no wobble or cracked joints
Dimensions fit your space and doorways

items.name: Appliances & Tools
items.intro: Appliances and power tools are bought on function. See them work, check recalls, and price around repair costs.
buy: See it plugged in and running.
Check model numbers for recalls.
Ask for age; most major appliances list a manufacture date on the plate.
For gas appliances, use a qualified installer.
sell: Photograph the model/serial plate.
Clean thoroughly — appearance drives offers.
Offer a short in-person demo.
flags: Can't demonstrate it running
Missing safety guards on power tools
check: No open recall on model number
No leaks, burning smell or unusual noise

items.name: Clothing & Shoes
items.intro: Fashion resale is a brand-and-condition game. Fast fashion rarely pays the effort; quality brands and vintage do.
buy: Ask for measurements, not just the tag size.
Check seams, underarms, soles and heel wear.
For sneakers and designer items, insist on authentication or a platform that authenticates.
sell: Flat-lay plus on-body photos; show tags and flaws.
Use brand + item + size + colour in the title.
Bundle low-value pieces.
flags: Stock photos only
Prices that undercut every sold listing for a hyped item
check: Authentic (labels, stitching, materials) for branded items
No stains, holes, pilling or odour

items.name: Designer Bags, Watches & Jewelry
items.intro: Luxury resale lives and dies on authentication and provenance. Iconic pieces can hold most of their retail value; counterfeits are rampant.
buy: Buy where items are authenticated, or pay for independent authentication.
Ask for receipt, box, dust bag, cards and service papers.
For watches, check serial and reference numbers and service history.
sell: Get it authenticated first — it raises buyer confidence and price.
Photograph date codes, hardware, stitching and serials.
Consider consignment for hands-off selling.
flags: 'Authentic, no receipt, priced to sell fast'
Refuses close-up photos of serials/date codes
check: Serial / date code consistent with model and era

items.name: Baby & Kids Gear
items.intro: Kids outgrow gear fast, so the used market is huge — and so are the safety stakes. Recalls and current safety standards come first.
buy: Check every model against recall databases before buying.
Avoid used car seats unless you know the full history and expiry date.
Never use drop-side cribs or inclined sleepers.
Make sure all parts and instructions are present.
sell: Check recalls before listing — don't sell recalled products.
Include model number and manufacture date in photos.
Clean thoroughly and list complete sets.
flags: Car seat without label/expiry date
Missing hardware on cribs or strollers
check: Car seat: not expired, never in a crash
No cracks, sharp edges or loose parts

items.name: Books & Textbooks
items.intro: Textbook value collapses when a new edition ships; collectible books go the other way. The ISBN tells you almost everything.
buy: Match the ISBN and edition your course requires.
Check for access-code dependency.
Look for water damage and heavy highlighting.
sell: Compare buyback quotes by ISBN before semester end.
Sell immediately after finals — prices drop over the summer.
Bundle cheap paperbacks.
flags: International edition sold as US edition without disclosure

items.name: Musical Instruments & Audio
items.intro: Quality instruments hold value remarkably well, which makes used gear one of the best buys in the market — and one of the easiest to price using sold data.
buy: Play it plugged in and unplugged.
Check neck relief, frets and electronics crackle.
Verify serials for vintage claims.
sell: Use a music-gear price guide to set the price.
Photograph serials, headstock and any wear honestly.
Ship in a proper case or local-pickup only.
flags: Vintage claim with no serial or documentation
check: Electronics: no crackle, all positions work

items.name: Sports & Outdoor Gear
items.intro: Specialised sports gear sells best to people who know the sport. Sizes and safety ratings matter more than brand.
buy: Know your size and spec before you shop.
Helmets: replace after any impact; check manufacture date.
Check for cracks on sticks, clubs, skis and boards.
sell: List size, flex, length and handedness in the title.
Sell seasonally: skis in autumn, golf in spring.
flags: Helmet with unknown crash history
check: Safety gear has no impact damage and is in date

items.name: Collectibles & Antiques
items.intro: Collectibles are priced by rarity, condition and provenance — and by realized sale prices, not asking prices. Research before you buy or sell.
buy: Research realized prices, not listings.
Ask for provenance and any grading certificates.
Learn the common reproductions in your category.
sell: Identify maker's marks and edition details.
Grade condition honestly; consider professional grading for high-value items.
Auction formats work well for rare items with competing buyers.
flags: Story-heavy listing with no marks or documentation
